title: Langtang Lirung ice-rock avalanche and Trishuli debris flood
outcome: Approximately 0.2 km2 of ice and rock detached and fell about 1.2 km, impacting at roughly 50 m/s. Frictional melting generated a debris flood down the Trishuli. 13 hydropower plants were knocked offline; remains were recovered up to 240 km downstream.
lesson: The operational early-warning system was calibrated for monsoon river flooding and was not connected to any ground-motion input. Upstream hydrological stations were destroyed by the surge before they could report. Detection had to come from the slope, not the river.
source_note: Figures as reported in the immediate aftermath; verify against the final official assessment before citing publicly.

title: Assam south-bank tributary floods
outcome: Cloudbursts upstream sent sudden surges down the Dikhow and Dhansiri immediately before the Brahmaputra mainstem peaked, creating a drainage bottleneck. Over 2,000 villages affected and 1.7-1.8 lakh people impacted.
lesson: Mechanically the classic case rainfall-trend monitoring handles well. The gap was not detection but reach: rural and dispersed communities received warnings late or by word of mouth.
source_note: Figures as reported; verify against official state disaster authority bulletins before citing publicly.

title: Chamoli rock-ice avalanche, Rishiganga / Dhauliganga
outcome: A wedge of rock and glacier ice detached from Ronti peak in midwinter and became a debris flow that destroyed the Rishiganga plant and overwhelmed the Tapovan-Vishnugad tunnel.
lesson: Occurred in dry winter conditions with no rainfall precursor whatsoever. The collapse was recorded on regional seismic networks minutes before the flow reached the downstream plants - a lead time nobody was positioned to use.
source_note: Extensively analysed in the peer-reviewed literature.

title: Seti River flash flood, Annapurna IV collapse
outcome: A rock and ice avalanche from the Annapurna IV massif produced a sudden debris-laden surge down the Seti gorge under a clear sky, killing people bathing and working along the riverbank.
lesson: The canonical 'clear-sky flood'. Downstream communities had no reason to expect water because there was no rain to see. Any warning had to originate from the mountain itself.
source_note: Widely studied; seismic records of the initial collapse exist.

title: South Lhonak Lake glacial lake outburst flood, Teesta basin
outcome: South Lhonak Lake breached after a slope failure entered the lake, sending a surge down the Teesta that destroyed the Teesta-III dam at Chungthang and swept downstream settlements.
lesson: A recognised, mapped, monitored hazard that still produced a catastrophic surprise, because monitoring was not wired to an alert path that reached the valley in minutes.
source_note: Official assessments and satellite analyses available.

title: Kedarnath disaster, Chorabari lake breach and extreme rainfall
outcome: Days of extreme rainfall combined with the breach of Chorabari lake produced a debris flood through Kedarnath town at the height of pilgrimage season.
lesson: A compound event: both channels were active at once. A system watching only one would have caught part of it and badly understated the total.
source_note: Death toll figures vary widely between official and independent estimates.

title: Jure landslide and Sunkoshi river dam
outcome: A massive hillside failure buried a village and dammed the Sunkoshi, creating an impounded lake that threatened a far larger outburst downstream for weeks.
lesson: Inverts the usual pattern: the immediate danger was the river STOPPING. Discharge dropping sharply below normal is itself an alarm, which a threshold-exceedance system reads as 'all clear'.
source_note: Documented by ICIMOD and the Nepal Army response.

title: Melamchi debris flood, Indrawati basin
outcome: Intense upper-catchment rainfall mobilised stored glacial and landslide sediment, producing a debris flood far larger than the rainfall alone would suggest, which wrecked the Melamchi water supply headworks.
lesson: Rainfall was the trigger but stored sediment was the amplifier. Rainfall-to-discharge models that ignore catchment sediment state systematically understate the peak.

title: Assam and Barak valley floods
outcome: Prolonged monsoon rainfall flooded large parts of the Barak and Brahmaputra valleys, displacing millions across multiple districts.
lesson: Detection worked. Evacuation logistics and alert reach into rural areas did not. This is a last-mile problem, not a sensing problem.

title: Assam monsoon floods
outcome: Successive monsoon waves flooded most of the Brahmaputra valley including large parts of Kaziranga National Park.
lesson: Slow-onset and highly predictable in mechanism. The value of a warning system here is lead time measured in days, and the binding constraint is who actually receives it.
